population.definition: Population of the Municipality of Tunis (commune de Tunis) recorded in the 2024 general census (Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat, census date 6 November 2024) conducted by the Institut National de la Statistique (INS) of Tunisia, tabulated via citypopulation.de. The Governorate of Tunis counted 1,075,306 residents, and the wider metropolitan conurbation (Grand Tunis, spanning Tunis, Ariana, Ben Arous and Manouba) counted 2,644,640 residents.

source.title: Tunisia: Governorates, Major Cities & Communes (Census 2024)
source.publisher: CityPopulation (credits Institut National de la Statistique, Tunisie)

facts.claim: Tunis was established as an Arab city around 698 AD by Umayyad general Hasan ibn al-Nu'man following the fall of Byzantine Carthage, centering on the founding of the Ez-Zitouna Mosque.

source.title: Grande Mosquée Zitouna
source.quote: founded around 698 CE after the conquest of Carthage

facts.claim: Under the Hafsid dynasty (1229–1574), Tunis became the capital of Ifriqiya and one of the wealthiest intellectual and commercial metropolises of the Mediterranean and Islamic worlds.

source.title: Medina of Tunis
source.quote: Under the Almohads and the Hafsids, from the 12th to the 16th century, Tunis was considered one of the greatest and wealthiest cities in the Islamic world

facts.claim: The renowned polymath and founder of sociology, Ibn Khaldun, was born in Tunis in 1332 and began his studies at the university-mosque of Ez-Zitouna.

source.title: Grande Mosquée Zitouna
source.quote: Ibn Khaldun studied and taught at Ez-Zitouna

facts.claim: In 1881 France established a protectorate over Tunisia, initiating the development of the modern European grid city east of Bab El Bhar along Avenue de la Marine (now Avenue Habib Bourguiba).

source.title: Théâtre municipal de Tunis
source.quote: development of the modern European city under the protectorate

facts.claim: Tunis became the capital of the sovereign Republic of Tunisia upon independence in 1956 and the abolition of the monarchy in 1957.

timeline.claim: Hasan ibn al-Nu'man founds Arab Tunis and initiates the Ez-Zitouna Mosque.
The Hafsid dynasty establishes Tunis as the royal capital of Ifriqiya.

source.title: Medina of Tunis
source.quote: became the capital of the Hafsid kingdom

timeline.claim: Historian and philosopher Ibn Khaldun is born in the Medina of Tunis.

source.title: Grande Mosquée Zitouna
source.quote: Ibn Khaldun was born in Tunis in 1332

timeline.claim: Ottoman forces under Sinan Pasha capture Tunis, integrating it into the Ottoman Empire.
The Bardo National Museum opens in the former palace of the Husainid beys.
The Art Nouveau Théâtre Municipal de Tunis opens on Avenue Habib Bourguiba.
Tunisia regains independence; Tunis is confirmed as sovereign capital.
Mass demonstrations along Avenue Habib Bourguiba culminate in the departure of Ben Ali.

source.title: Théâtre municipal de Tunis
source.quote: symbolic gathering place during the 2011 revolution

places.name: Bardo National Museum
places.what: The national museum of Tunisia, housed in an ornate 15th- to 19th-century beylical palace in the suburb of Le Bardo. Established in 1888, it holds one of the world's most extensive collections of Roman mosaics, including the 3rd-century portrait of Virgil with the muses of tragedy and history.

facts.label: Famous mosaic
facts.value: Virgil composing the Aeneid (3rd century AD)

places.name: Ez-Zitouna Mosque
places.what: The historic Great Mosque and university in the heart of the Medina of Tunis, founded around 698 CE. Its prayer hall features approximately 160 antique columns reclaimed from ancient Carthage, and for centuries it served as one of the oldest universities in the Islamic world.

facts.label: Distinction
facts.value: Historic university where Ibn Khaldun studied and taught

source.title: Grande Mosquée Zitouna
source.quote: Ibn Khaldun studied and taught here

places.name: Avenue Habib Bourguiba
places.what: The broad central avenue of modern Tunis running from Bab El Bhar to Lake Tunis. Lined with ficus trees, cafes, the 1897 Cathedral of St. Vincent de Paul, and the 1902 Art Nouveau Théâtre Municipal by Jean-Émile Resplandy, it was the focal public gathering point of the 2011 Tunisian revolution.

places.name: Dar Lasram
places.what: An 18th- to early 19th-century aristocratic palace in the Medina of Tunis, built between 1812 and 1819 for Hamouda Lasram. Acquired by the municipality in the 1960s, it serves as the headquarters of the Association de Sauvegarde de la Médina (ASM).

source.title: Dar Lasram et l'Association de Sauvegarde de la Médina de Tunis
